//: The core's .claude/settings.json (layer 5). Two hard paths (Spec §12): the hooks (deterministic guardrails before/after an action) and permissions.deny (a blocklist evaluated by the permission engine itself). Structure per the Claude Code documentation. Hooks are invoked through bash explicitly: under Windows/PowerShell, a .sh called directly runs NOTHING, without an error, and the guard would fail open in silence (real install, 2026-08-06). This file and .claude/hooks/ change through upgrade.sh or by the user's hand, never through the agent's file tools (the deny below, and guard.sh rule 4).

permissions.//: Second hard path (Spec §12): a blocklist evaluated before any call, redundant with guard.sh by design (defense in depth), not a replacement. An Edit(...) rule covers every file-editing tool (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit); Claude Code ignores Write(...) rules with a warning, so none is written. The guardrail's own files are denied so that the agent cannot rewrite what constrains it.
